# Runink

> Runink makes four separate products: Runink FACE for logistics, freight, claims and operations teams; Runink TIDE for engineering, platform and data teams; Runink PULSE for marketing teams; and Runink River, a free, open-source workstation operating system for data, analytics and AI work. FACE, TIDE and PULSE are each sold on their own subscription.

Runink TIDE was called Runink CORE until October 2026; links to the old
/products/core/ address still arrive at the TIDE page.

## What each product is


### Runink FACE

For logistics, freight, claims and operations teams. FACE reads the invoices, orders, carrier records and claim files you already keep, finds the overcharge, the claim about to expire and the broken rule, and drafts the next step for a named person to approve. It runs on your own servers or cloud account, or on Runink's shared machines to start, and no outside AI service is called.

- Product page: https://runink.org/products/face/
- Prices: https://runink.org/pricing/ — The operational jobs Runink FACE is built for, and what a licence to run them costs. You pay for the number of people who use it, and choose where the work runs: on Runink's shared machines, in your own cloud account, or on your own premises.

### Runink TIDE

Runink TIDE takes the repeat questions off engineering, platform and data teams: what broke and why, whether a fix shipped, which number is right, who changed what. Run it on your own servers, in your own cloud account, or on Runink's shared machines to start. Helpers propose; a person approves.

- Product page: https://runink.org/products/tide/
- Prices: https://runink.org/products/tide-pricing/ — What a licence to run Runink TIDE costs. You choose where it runs: on Runink's shared machines, priced per person; in your own cloud account, priced per node; or on your own premises, priced with you. There is no second bill: TIDE never charges a percentage of anything it finds, fixes or ships.

### Runink PULSE

Runink PULSE is marketing software your own team runs: it finds leads, drafts the replies, campaigns and follow-ups, and shows which channel brings customers in. Your team decides what goes out. Priced per seat.

- Product page: https://runink.org/products/pulse/

### Runink River

Runink River is a free, open-source workstation operating system for data, analytics and AI work on hardware you own. The disk is encrypted, a bad update rolls back with one reboot, nothing gets in unless you open it, and there is no per-seat licence.

- Product page: https://runink.org/river/

## True of FACE, TIDE and PULSE

Each is sold on its own subscription, priced by the person or by the machine
it runs on, never as a bundle. Every drafted action waits for a named person;
approving it is what sends it, and who approved it is recorded. Each one can
run on Runink's shared machines, in the customer's own cloud account, or on the
customer's own premises.

We have not been audited against SOC 2, ISO 27001 or any other framework by an
external auditor. The software is built against them and will tell you what it
checked; it does not claim a certification it does not hold. There are no
published customer results, case studies or return-on-investment figures on
this site, and that is deliberate — where a number would go, the pages name the
measure and say where to find it in your own systems instead.

## The long documents


- [Runink FACE — Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine](https://runink.org/blog/whitepapers/runink-face/): Scattered across a dozen systems that were never designed to talk to each other. FACE assembles it, works out what the combined picture means, and produces a specific, reviewable recommendation with the underlying records attached — for a named person to approve.
- [Runink FACE — Logistics & Supply Chain Whitepaper](https://runink.org/blog/whitepapers/runink-face-logistics/): Scattered across a dozen systems that were never designed to talk to each other. FACE assembles it, works out what the combined picture means, and produces a specific, reviewable recommendation with the underlying records attached — for a named person to approve.
- [Runink TIDE — The operations layer for companies that keep their own data](https://runink.org/blog/whitepapers/runink-tide/): The operations layer a company runs on its own machines. One console shows whether the platform is healthy and your changes shipped, what your AI models and agents are allowed to do, what your data holds and where spending goes wrong, and turns a written brief into a working application with a person approving each step.
- [Runink PULSE — Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine](https://runink.org/blog/whitepapers/runink-pulse/): One application a marketing team operates directly. It audits your website and social presence, researches your market, prospects the public web for leads, and writes the material that carries somebody from first hearing of you to buying from you — staging every draft with a status and an approve against it, on channels that stay disarmed until you arm them.
- [Runink TIDE and Atlas for Banking](https://runink.org/blog/whitepapers/runink-tide-atlas-banking/): Four problems every bank carries, and for each one the TIDE console pages its people would open: who owns the problem, what each page gives them, and where in their own systems they find today's baseline.
- [Runink TIDE and Atlas — Continuous oversight, with a second opinion built in](https://runink.org/blog/whitepapers/runink-tide-atlas/): Atlas, from Logical Leap, is a set of screens for watching capital spending and data quality. TIDE runs those screens as its Intelligence pages, on the company's own hardware and the company's own data. This paper goes through each Atlas page in turn, then shows how the rest of TIDE adds a second opinion, a record in which any edit shows, and a person's approval before anything changes.

## Where it fits


- [Logistics & Supply Chain](https://runink.org/industries/logistics-supply-chain/): Held customs entries, freight claims that expire unfiled, cold chain read after the write-off, and demand that grew on the way up the chain. How Runink puts the evidence in front of the person who can act on it.
- [Insurance](https://runink.org/industries/insurance/): Claims decisioning, reserving and reinsurance recovery, delegated authority and conduct evidence. How Runink FACE sets the rule as written beside the logic your systems actually run, and sorts every rule into aligned, drift, shadow or missing.
- [Banking & Financial Services](https://runink.org/industries/banking-financial-services/): Payment instruction integrity, third-party risk, decision governance, fee and interest calculation. The Runink TIDE and Atlas oversight arrangement: an assessment platform produces findings, and TIDE judges each one on separate credentials before a person is asked to act.
- [Telecom](https://runink.org/industries/telecom/): Revenue assurance, rating and billing, interconnect settlement, network capital programmes. The Runink TIDE and Atlas oversight arrangement applied to two records that ought to agree, at the transaction.
- [Marketing](https://runink.org/industries/marketing/): Weeks-long turnaround, a stack that does not talk to itself, and effort that never compounds. Runink PULSE puts one diagnosis behind every channel, with a named person approving every draft.

## Worked scenarios


- [Cold Chain and Yard Safety](https://runink.org/use-cases/cold-chain-safety/): A container drifts warm overnight and nobody opens the door until morning. What the yard camera already sees, read against the handover record and the paperwork the consignment travels with.
- [Customer Data Privacy and Emissions Reporting](https://runink.org/use-cases/compliance/): Operating a system quietly writes personal data into its own logs, and the emissions report takes a quarter to assemble. What the software reads for each, what it hands to the person accountable, and where a check it could not run says so.
- [Freight Claims and Port Charges](https://runink.org/use-cases/claims-recovery/): Claims expire because assembling one takes a morning. The entry, the hold, the missing documents, the days held and the per-day charge arrive already gathered and joined, so a person only has to judge whether the case holds.
- [Re-Running the Route After the Day Has Changed](https://runink.org/use-cases/route-optimization/): The plan that was optimal at six in the morning is not optimal by ten. Nobody re-runs it, because re-running it means re-planning a day by hand. This is about making the second run cost nothing.
- [Returns and What to Do With Them](https://runink.org/use-cases/responsive-reverse-logistics/): A returned item is worth the most on the day it comes back. The call on where it goes — shelf, refurbishment, recycling or disposal — is drafted at the scan, from a written-down policy that gives the same grade the same answer every time.
- [Stock Cover and Supplier Planning](https://runink.org/use-cases/fulfillment-optimization/): Most stockout warnings arrive after the safety stock is already gone, which leaves you paying for air freight. The point is to see it while there is still time to order normally.
- [Talking to Drivers Without a Screen](https://runink.org/use-cases/voice-dispatch/): The person who knows a load is late is the one who cannot type. Asking and answering out loud gets the fact onto the record while the truck keeps moving, and the desk still makes the change.
- [Testing a Plan Before You Commit to It](https://runink.org/use-cases/hypothesis-lab/): A port shuts and you have a day to pick a new route. State the change as a hypothesis and the rules it touches, and get back the case laid out — which rules it collides with, in what order, and what someone would have to believe for the plan to hold. The decision stays with the person accountable for it.
- [The Picture Nobody Has Time to Assemble](https://runink.org/use-cases/supply-chain-visibility/): The facts are in four systems in four formats, and joining them takes a morning nobody has. So the picture that would let somebody act only ever gets assembled after the fact, for the meeting that reviews it.
- [When Demand Turns Before the Plan Does](https://runink.org/use-cases/demand-forecasting/): A line starts moving weeks before the reorder point does. By the time the plan catches up the cover is gone, and the difference is paid in air freight. This is about reading the turn while it is still a forecasting problem.
- [Which Clause Governs This, and Who Checked](https://runink.org/use-cases/paralegal-review/): A routine question settled by a paragraph takes a day and a half to answer, so it gets answered from memory instead. The clause and the record arrive together, cited. The reading is the software's. The judgement is not.
- [Your Adjusters Spend the Day Gathering, Not Deciding](https://runink.org/use-cases/insurance-underwriting/): The policy wording, the loss report, the reserve history and the authority limit for a claim that size sit in four places. They arrive joined, with a drafted next step and the reading it rests on. The underwriter still decides.

## Shorter pieces

Articles on the operational problems behind the documents above — held customs
entries, freight claims inside their filing window, returns that cost more to
handle than the goods, demurrage, cross-docking, cold chain, procurement
visibility. Index: https://runink.org/blog/

## Company

- [About Runink](https://runink.org/company/): What Runink is for: reading the records a company already keeps, and turning them into decisions its own people can defend.
- [Trust & Compliance](https://runink.org/trust/): How Runink keeps a person in charge of every decision, where the models run, how data is kept apart, how releases are signed, how our controls line up with SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 31000, ISO/IEC 42001 and PCI DSS v4.0, and how to report a security problem.
